title: Storyville and the African roots of jazz rhythm
summary: He describes Storyville as the red light district presented as the musical home of jazz, and says the rhythm came from Africa via the river.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Now, Storyville. Was Storyville everything that legend says it's like?

Yeah, I think so. But they put it in a nice way. Storyville, it used to be the red light district. It was. Yeah. But for modern eyes of the jazz and things, kids couldn't pick up on that. They didn't know it was Dolmott. So they just put Storyville from the musical end of it, see? And that's where jazz began, then? Was it going to drift up the Mississippi right up to Chicago? Right up to Mississippi on the levees and the plantations and all those melodies. And that rhythm, see? And before that, come to think of it, it was instilled in me that my great-grandfather, grandmother, way back there, they brought that rhythm from Africa to New Orleans. Oh, boy. Because I saw it when I went back. You ain't never seen so many rhythms. And different tribes, everyone had a different rhythm.
